newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN BEAT DORTMUND TO REACH LEAGUE CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN BEAT DORTMUND TO REACH LEAGUE CUP FINAL.

text.p: Bayern Munich warmed up for the new season with an impressive 2-0 victory over European Cup winners Borussia Dortmund on Wednesday to reach the final of the inaugural German League Cup.
Goals from new Brazilian signing Giovane Elber and international defender Markus Babbel helped the Bundesliga champions move towards a clash with VfB Stuttgart in Saturday's final in Leverkusen.
Stuttgart beat Karlsruhe 3-0 on Tuesday in the other semifinal of the lucrative competition which brings together the top six teams of last year's league championship.
The League Cup has replaced the traditional Super Cup between the champions and the Cup winners as the curtain raiser to the season which starts next month.
Elber, who joined from Stuttgart for 12.5 million marks ($6.9 million), put Bayern in front with a shot from just outside the penalty area after 29 minutes of the Augsburg game.
A header by Babbel from a cross by new French signing Bixente Lizarazu allowed the Munich club to seal the win and make sure of 750,000 marks ($416,000) in prize money.
"We're not ready yet but I liked what I saw tonight," Bayern's Italian coach Giovanni Trapattoni. "I'm pleased with the spirit, the mentality of the players. That's promising."
His Borussia counterpart, fellow Italian Nevio Scala who has just taken charge in Dortmund, was not too concerned by the defeat.
"Of course, we would have preferred to win but it's not dramatic," he said. "The season hasn't really started yet."
